# relay_migration_check (Data Source)

Checks whether a PostgreSQL database outside Relay can be migrated into Relay. Each read runs a new check against the source, from the network path the migration will use, and waits for it to finish, up to the `read` timeout, 10 minutes by default. The password and connection string are kept in the Terraform state like every data source argument. There is no `relay_migration` resource: a migration is run from the Relay CLI or the dashboard, once the check has no blockers. Reading it needs the `database_migration` feature enabled for the organization.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "source_database_url" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

check "orders_database_can_migrate" {
  data "relay_migration_check" "orders" {
    workspace_id   = relay_workspace.prod.id
    cloud          = "aws"
    region         = "us-east-1"
    target_version = "17"
    mode           = "online"

    source = {
      connection_string = var.source_database_url
    }
  }

  assert {
    condition     = !data.relay_migration_check.orders.has_blockers
    error_message = "The orders database cannot be migrated to Relay online: ${join("; ", [for r in data.relay_migration_check.orders.results : r.message if r.level == "blocker"])}"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `source` (Attributes) The database to check. Set `connection_string`, or `host`, `database` and `username`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--source))
- `workspace_id` (String) Workspace the target belongs to.

### Optional

- `cloud` (String) Cloud of the planned target. Needs `region`, and cannot be set with `database_id`.
- `database_id` (String) Existing database the source would migrate into. Set it, or `cloud` and `region` for a target that does not exist yet.
- `mode` (String) How the migration would move the data: `online`, the default, or `offline`. It decides which results count for `has_blockers` and `acknowledgements`.
- `region` (String) Region of the planned target. Needs `cloud`.
- `target_storage` (String) Storage of the planned target, for example `100Gi`.
- `target_version` (String) PostgreSQL version of the planned target, for example `17`.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `acknowledgements` (List of String) The acknowledgements that the warnings applying to `mode` need before a migration can be created.
- `expires_at` (String) When the check stops being valid for creating a migration, RFC 3339.
- `facts` (Attributes) What the check read from the source. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--facts))
- `has_blockers` (Boolean) Whether a `blocker` result applies to `mode`: one for every mode, or for that mode only. For example, a huge interval value blocks `online` only.
- `id` (String) Check ID.
- `modes` (List of String) The modes the source can migrate in, `online` and `offline`.
- `results` (Attributes List) What the check found, one entry per rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--results))

<a id="nestedatt--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `source`

Optional:

- `acknowledge_unverified_tls` (Boolean) Accept that `ssl_mode = "require"` does not verify the source's certificate.
- `ca_pem` (String) PEM bundle that verifies the source's certificate. Without it, a host on AWS RDS or Aurora is verified with the provider's public CA bundle.
- `connection_string` (String, Sensitive) A `postgres://` or `postgresql://` URI with the user, password, host, port and database. `sslmode` may be `verify-full` or `require`.
- `database` (String) Database to check.
- `host` (String) Host of the source.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password of `username`.
- `port` (Number) Port of the source. Defaults to `5432`.
- `ssl_mode` (String) How the source's certificate is verified: `verify-full`, the default, or `require`, which needs `acknowledge_unverified_tls`. Cannot be set when `connection_string` has a `sslmode`.
- `username` (String) User the check connects as.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--facts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `facts`

Read-Only:

- `database_size_bytes` (Number) Size of the source database, in bytes.
- `encoding` (String) Database encoding.
- `largest_row_bytes` (Number) Size of the largest row found, in bytes.
- `max_slot_wal_keep_size` (String) The source's `max_slot_wal_keep_size` setting.
- `owner` (String) Owner of the source database.
- `provider` (String) Managed provider the source runs on, empty when none was recognized.
- `server_version` (String) PostgreSQL version of the source.
- `wal_bytes_per_second` (Number) WAL the source writes per second, in bytes.


<a id="nestedatt--results"></a>
### Nested Schema for `results`

Read-Only:

- `acknowledgement` (String) The acknowledgement that accepts this warning when a migration is created, for example `timetz`, empty when none is needed.
- `fix` (String) How to resolve it, empty when there is nothing to fix.
- `level` (String) `pass`, `warning` or `blocker`.
- `message` (String) What was found.
- `mode` (String) `online` or `offline` when the result applies to that mode only, empty when it applies to every mode.
- `name` (String) Rule that produced the result.
